summary: R-6 flat cab on a 10-ft concrete base replaced a 1929 cabin on Middle Fork Peak in Idaho in 1962; the summer staffing status is disputed between sources.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on 10-ft concrete base (built 1962)

staffing.status: disputed: staffed each summer (Forest Service, page last updated May 22, 2025); not staffed 2025-2026 (Idaho Fire Lookouts)
staffing.as_of: Forest Service page last updated May 22, 2025; Idaho Fire Lookouts 2025-2026

access.note: Forest Service road to the summit; the 2018 climbing guide says a 4WD vehicle with exceptionally good tires is required. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as drive-up.

visit.trail_note: Per the 2018 climbing guide: a route starting at Panther Creek follows FS-112 about 15 miles to a 4-way junction, then 14.25 miles to the road end below the summit. A trail from the Middle Fork Salmon River gains about 5,000 feet.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Salmon-Challis National Forest (Salmon-Cobalt Ranger District)

events.note: First lookout on the site, a cabin; sources disagree on its type (DuBois cabin per NHLR, R-4 log cabin per Idaho Fire Lookouts)
Replaced by the present R-6 flat cab on a 10-ft concrete base

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service page, last updated May 22, 2025, says the Middle Fork lookout is staffed each summer, and NHLR says the same. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as not staffed for 2025-2026. Both are reported and the current status is treated as unsettled.
NHLR calls the first 1929 cabin a DuBois cabin. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists an R-4 log cabin. Both are reported; the type is not settled.

Most sources give 1929. A 1982 account quoted in a 2018 climbing guide places the site in the 1919-1923 fire plans and mentions an early 1920s structure. The story reports this and does not resolve it.
NHLR places the site on the Salmon National Forest. The Forest Service page uses the Salmon-Challis National Forest name for the unit. The story uses the name the agency page uses.

notes_for_editor: Staffing is the main dispute: Forest Service (last updated May 22, 2025) says staffed each summer; Idaho Fire Lookouts says not staffed 2025-2026. The 1929 vs early-1920s first-structure date and the DuBois vs R-4 cabin type are both unresolved and reported as such. No notable fire found in these sources. Record height_m 3.0 matches the 10-ft concrete base, not total tower height; kind two_story left as is. Access and road details come from a 2018 climbing guide and should be rechecked. Idaho Fire Lookouts staff-name list omitted on purpose (private individuals). No new photos recorded.
